title: X Feed Digest
summary: Gemini 3 Deep Think received a major upgrade, pushing new reasoning benchmarks and signaling Google’s focus on science-grade model performance.
OpenAI’s real-time coding push continues with GPT‑5.3‑Codex‑Spark, while open-source challengers like MiniMax M2.5 claim frontier-level productivity at lower cost.
Research is shifting from bigger context windows to smarter retrieval: DeepMind’s Recursive Language Models propose code-driven navigation to avoid context rot.
AI capital and infrastructure bets are intensifying (Alphabet’s long-dated debt, Anthropic’s oversized raise) amid broader market volatility and policy shakeups.

items.title: @Google: Gemini 3 Deep Think upgrade
items.body: Google says Gemini 3 Deep Think was upgraded for science, research, and engineering, hitting 84.6% on ARC‑AGI‑2 and setting a new bar on Humanity’s Last Exam. It’s framed as a specialized reasoning mode for R&D-grade work.

items.title: @OpenAIDevs: GPT‑5.3‑Codex‑Spark
items.body: OpenAI introduced GPT‑5.3‑Codex‑Spark, a real‑time coding model rolling out as a research preview for ChatGPT Pro via the Codex app, CLI, and IDE extension.

items.title: @MiniMax_AI: M2.5 open‑source model
items.body: MiniMax launched M2.5, an open‑source frontier model claiming strong coding/search/tool‑calling benchmarks and faster execution aimed at long‑horizon agent workflows.

items.title: @simplifyinAI: Recursive Language Models
items.body: DeepMind’s RLM paper proposes navigation‑based memory: models write code to search and slice data instead of loading huge windows, sharply improving multi‑document research scores and reducing context rot.

items.title: @ai: Karpathy’s microGPT
items.body: Andrej Karpathy released microGPT—an end‑to‑end GPT implementation in 243 lines of pure Python—meant as a readable reference for how LLMs actually work.

items.title: @WatcherGuru: $1T market cap wipeout
items.body: WatcherGuru reports roughly $1T was wiped from the U.S. stock market in a single day, highlighting the sharp volatility in recent sessions.

items.title: @BarackObama: Endangerment finding repeal
items.body: Obama says the administration repealed the EPA endangerment finding—the legal basis for emissions limits—warning it weakens climate protections and public health safeguards.

items.title: @KKaWSB: Alphabet issues ultra‑long debt
items.body: Alphabet reportedly issued Swiss‑franc bonds and a rare 100‑year GBP bond after a $20B U.S. debt sale, aiming to fund up to $185B in long‑term AI infrastructure.

items.title: @techeconomyana: Anthropic’s $30B raise
items.body: A report claims Anthropic’s funding round swelled to $30B (from an initial $10B plan) with ARR around $14B, signaling huge investor appetite for leading AI labs.

items.title: @fxtrader: OpenAI vs. DeepSeek
items.body: OpenAI told a U.S. House committee it observed DeepSeek‑linked accounts attempting to bypass access limits and distill outputs from U.S. models, per a reported memo.

items.title: @KKaWSB: The Cantillon effect
items.body: A concise primer on the Cantillon effect: inflation redistributes wealth toward those who receive new money first, while late recipients bear higher prices.

items.title: @lxjost: ROAS can mislead
items.body: A short warning for ecommerce teams: a rising ROAS can mask deteriorating customer quality, making the headline metric more dangerous than it looks.

items.title: @pingzhang632: Tracked iPhone to Senegal
items.body: A German blogger used Find My to trace a stolen iPhone to Senegal, then traveled there and—with local help—eventually recovered it from a shop.
